Apple Watch Battery Life Tips
articles.summary: To conserve battery life on an Apple Watch, users can check its battery health status and adjust their usage patterns, including enabling Low Power Mode to extend battery life by several days.
articles.content: Apple Watch users often find themselves struggling to squeeze out every last bit of battery life from their device, especially on days when they need it most. The company claims that its latest models can last for up to 24 hours on a single charge, but real-world results often vary greatly depending on individual usage patterns. Apple's own estimates are based on a combination of 300 time checks, 15 minutes of app use, six hours of sleep tracking, and other factors. To give your Apple Watch an extra boost, it's worth checking its battery health status to see if it's still performing within normal parameters. You can do this by navigating to Settings > Battery > Battery Health on your watch. If you find that your Apple Watch's battery life is significantly depleted, it may be time to consider bringing it in for a replacement. However, power users might prefer to opt for the Apple Watch Ultra 4, which boasts a larger battery and is better equipped to handle demanding usage. Making small adjustments to how you use your watch throughout the day can also help eke out more battery life. This includes enabling certain toggles and being mindful of your app usage and other power-hungry features. When your Apple Watch's battery life starts to dwindle, turning on Low Power Mode can be a lifesaver. To activate this feature, press the side button and tap on the battery percentage in the top right corner of the screen. A notification will appear with an information card that provides instructions for enabling Low Power Mode. Scroll down and select "Turn On" to proceed, or choose to keep the mode active for one, two, or three days if you anticipate being away from a charger during that time. Alternatively, you can access Low Power Mode by navigating to Settings > Battery on your Apple Watch. This will allow you to toggle the feature on and off as needed. When Low Power Mode is activated, several changes become apparent immediately. The Always On display is disabled, along with the Wrist Flick and Double Tap gestures. However, your watch's screen will still light up automatically when you raise your wrist. Background heart rate and blood oxygen measurements are paused while in Low Power Mode, but you can use their respective apps to take manual readings at any time. This does mean that low, high, or irregular heart rate notifications will be disabled, which may be a concern for some users. Apple notes that Siri requests on the Apple Watch can take longer to process when the device is running in Low Power Mode. Additionally, Live Activities and complications on your watch face will update less frequently, and scrolling may become slightly more sluggish as a result. When using your Apple Watch in areas with Wi-Fi connectivity, it's a good idea to opt for this internet connection instead of relying on cellular data. This is because connecting to Wi-Fi can help conserve battery life, which is especially useful when you're not actively using the watch. However, if you do need to use cellular connectivity, make sure your Apple Watch and iPhone are connected. A tiny green phone icon in Control Center on your Apple Watch indicates that this connection has been established over Bluetooth. To further extend your Apple Watch's battery life, consider enabling Airplane Mode when you're not actively using the device for an extended period. This can be found in either Control Center or through the Settings app. Despite the limitations of being disconnected from the internet, your Apple Watch still offers a range of features that don't require online access. These include tracking workouts, playing stored music or podcasts, making purchases with Apple Pay and monitoring sleep patterns. The built-in apps on your Apple Watch also continue to function as usual when offline. This includes Alarms, Timers, Medications and Voice Memos, among others. Newer Apple Watch models come equipped with improved speakers that allow for direct music playback, while companion app installations on the watch are automatically synced from the paired iPhone if available. The convenience of having multiple apps installed on your Apple Watch comes at a cost - battery life. To conserve power, it's essential to manage app usage and notifications effectively. Uninstalling unused apps from your watch directly doesn't remove them from your iPhone, so consider deleting them from the watch if you're not using them frequently. For occasional use apps that don't require constant updates, turn off Background App Refresh by navigating to Settings > General > Background App Refresh. Disabling Background App Refresh entirely will affect all apps on your watch, but this might be a necessary step to save battery life. If you're unsure which apps are consuming the most power, monitoring their usage can help identify areas for improvement. Customizing app notifications is another way to reduce battery drain. By default, disabled iPhone app notifications also apply to your Apple Watch, but you can adjust this setting through the Watch app on your iPhone. To fine-tune notification settings, navigate to Notifications in the Watch app and scroll down to the Mirror iPhone Alerts From section. Disable toggles for apps that don't need to send notifications to your watch, reducing vibrations and screen wake-ups throughout the day. Turning off Always On display is another option for those seeking more control over battery life. To do this, navigate to Settings > Display & Brightness > Always On on your Apple Watch and toggle the feature off. Covering your Apple Watch when not in use is a simple yet effective way to minimize screen-on time and save battery life. This habit can be developed by making it a point to always use your palm to cover the watch face after you've finished interacting with it. Another option worth exploring is disabling the Always On display, which can have a significant impact on battery life. According to testing, turning off this feature can extend battery life by 10 to 12 hours. This setting is located in the Display & Brightness menu within Settings. Preventing accidental screen activation is also crucial for conserving battery power. To do this, navigate to Settings > Gestures and toggle off Wake on Wrist Raise. Additionally, disabling gestures like Double Tap and Wrist Flick can help reduce unnecessary screen time. For users who regularly engage in longer workouts, configuring Low Power Mode to only kick in during specific exercises can be a viable option. This feature allows you to sacrifice some workout tracking features in exchange for extended battery life. In watchOS 27, the Workout app introduced two new options that enable this functionality. To take advantage of these options, open the Workout app and select an activity type. Tap on the Goals and Targets button in the top-right corner, then scroll down and tap on Extended to start tracking your activity with reduced features. Some workouts also offer a Max Extended Workout option, which further reduces GPS and heart rate measurements. This approach can help you strike a balance between workout tracking and battery conservation. Once you've completed an exercise, Low Power Mode will automatically turn off, allowing your watch to return to normal functionality. To activate automatic battery saver mode during workouts, head to Settings > Workout and toggle on Low Power Mode. This feature eliminates the need for manual selection of Extended Workout each time. With Low Power Mode activated, your Apple Watch will automatically switch to this setting once you've begun a workout, saving precious battery life. Once an exercise is completed, the watch returns to normal functionality, allowing for uninterrupted use until the next workout. articles.title: Disruptions at US Airports Cause Widespread Delays Across Multiple Airlines
articles.summary: A chaotic start to the Thanksgiving travel season was witnessed at several major US airports on Sunday, as a combination of technical issues and inclement weather caused widespread disruptions.
articles.content: A chaotic start to the Thanksgiving travel season was witnessed at several major US airports on Sunday, as a combination of technical issues and inclement weather caused widespread disruptions. Delta Air Lines reported an issue with its automated aircraft weight and balance calculation system, which triggered a series of delays at its Atlanta hub, Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. By 1pm EST, around 40% of all flights scheduled to depart from ATL had been delayed, according to FlightAware data. This included hundreds of both departing and arriving planes. Delta's spokesperson acknowledged the issue in a statement, revealing that the airline was resorting to manual workarounds to get flights airborne as soon as possible. However, the carrier's automated system remained offline, leaving passengers facing further uncertainty about their travel plans. The extent of Delta's operation affected by this disruption remains unclear at present. The Atlanta airport is one of the busiest in the world, and its congestion has already been compounded by a technical issue that will likely test Delta's ability to manage its operations over the coming days. Despite claims from the airline that it was using manual workarounds, thousands of passengers are still waiting for updates on their flights as the day wears on. Delta's cancellations remain relatively low despite ongoing disruptions, but regional subsidiary Endeavor Air has reported over 230 additional cancellations on its own, according to data from FlightAware. The airline is still struggling to provide updates to thousands of passengers waiting for flight information as the day wears on. In a statement, Delta expressed gratitude to customers for their patience and praised employees for their professionalism in handling the situation. Low cloud ceilings have been causing issues at various major airports, leading to delays and diversions of dozens of flights, with New York's LaGuardia Airport being one of the hardest hit. FlightAware data shows that nearly half of all departing and arriving flights from LGA were delayed on Sunday. Airline passengers affected by Delta's recent tech outage and severe weather may have grounds for seeking compensation or reimbursement for their expenses. According to Department of Transportation policy, if a flight is delayed or canceled due to circumstances beyond your control, such as the airline's own fault, you are entitled to assistance. This includes help with finding alternative travel arrangements, but it also extends to financial reimbursement for any additional costs incurred. If the delay is caused by bad weather, however, airlines typically do not offer compensation. In this case, passengers are often left to fend for themselves and seek reimbursement through other means if they have purchased a credit card that offers travel insurance. Keeping receipts of all expenses can be crucial in such situations. As Thanksgiving approaches, air travelers should be prepared for the possibility of disruptions, including those caused by severe weather. With airports expected to be busy over the next few days, passengers would do well to stay informed and plan ahead to minimize any inconvenience they may experience. As the Thanksgiving holiday approaches, travelers can expect a challenging time at airports. With next Sunday being potentially the busiest day to fly, air travel disruptions are likely to continue. The combination of Delta's recent tech outage and inclement weather is creating a perfect storm that may test the patience of even the most seasoned flyers. Airports will be under pressure to manage the influx of passengers, and it's essential for travelers to stay informed about flight schedules and any potential delays. With so many people taking to the skies, airports could be chaotic, and passengers would do well to plan ahead to minimize any inconvenience they may experience. The prospect of long wait times and crowded terminals is a daunting one. Despite these challenges, there are steps that can be taken to mitigate the impact of air travel disruptions. By staying up-to-date on flight information and being prepared for potential delays, travelers can reduce their stress levels and make the most of their journey. As the holiday season gets underway, it's clear that air travel will continue to pose significant challenges, but with planning and preparation, passengers can navigate these difficulties with greater ease. articles.title: Solar Panel Installation Costs Outweigh Benefits in Some Areas
articles.summary: Homeowners in certain regions may struggle to recoup their investment through savings on utility bills due to less favorable regulations or geography.
articles.content: The idea of adding solar panels to your home may seem like a great way to save money on electricity bills and boost the resale value of your property. However, there are several drawbacks to consider before making such an investment. These issues can be particularly pronounced for homeowners in states or regions with less favorable regulations or geography that doesn't receive optimal amounts of sunlight. In these cases, the benefits of solar panels may not outweigh the costs. The initial cost of installing a typical home solar power system is substantial, ranging from $20,000 to $27,000 before any incentives or rebates are applied. The national benchmark for this investment is $3.36 per watt, which can be a significant expense for many homeowners. Homeowners in certain areas may find that the upfront cost of installing solar panels is not justified by their electricity usage and rates. For instance, those living in states with relatively low electricity costs may struggle to recoup their investment through savings on their utility bills. The federal tax credit of 30 percent was previously available to help offset this expense, but it has been terminated by the Trump administration for now. This means that homeowners who had been counting on this incentive will need to weigh their options carefully before making a decision about solar panel installation. Homeowners in certain regions may find that installing solar panels has little effect on their electricity bills, particularly if they reside in a smaller dwelling, have a small household, or use energy-efficient appliances and consume minimal energy each month. To make an informed decision about investing in solar power, it's essential to research the incentives and rebates offered by your utility company. Not all companies provide net metering, which allows homeowners to receive credits for excess energy produced by their panels, potentially reducing or eliminating their monthly electric bill. The terms of these programs vary significantly from state to state, with some offering one-to-one power exchange, where homeowners are credited at the same retail rate they pay for electricity. Other states have buyback programs, reduced-rate structures, or net billing systems that credit homeowners a portion of what they pay for energy. When considering solar panels, geographic location is crucial. Areas with consistent sunlight and moderate temperatures tend to be ideal, as excessive heat or overcast weather can negatively impact panel performance and lifespan. The design of your home also plays a significant role in determining the feasibility of solar panels. Roofs that face south and are free from obstructions such as buildings, trees, or other objects are typically preferred for installation. If your roof is old, it may be necessary to install a new one before investing in solar panels, which can cost anywhere from $4,000 to over $35,000 depending on the size of your home and type of roof. In addition to these factors, homeowners should also consider the upfront costs associated with installing solar panels, including equipment, labor, and potential permitting fees. Homeowners considering solar panels often prioritize their visual appeal. Some may be hesitant to install traditional solar panels on a newly replaced roof, finding them unattractive and bulky. As an alternative, solar shingles are available, but they come with a hefty price tag. These shingles cost roughly twice as much per watt as standard solar panels. The installation costs for solar shingles can add up quickly, especially for larger homes. For example, installing solar shingles on a 2,500-square-foot house could cost between $52,500 and $62,500 before any available incentives are factored in. This price includes the cost of equipment, labor, and potential permitting fees. Another factor to consider is the reliability of solar power during outages. Many homeowners assume that their solar panels will automatically kick into gear when the grid goes down. However, this isn't the case without a battery backup system. These systems store excess energy generated by the solar panels and supply it to the home when needed. The cost of a single-battery backup system can be steep, ranging from $10,000 to $16,000 for basic models that power essential appliances like lights and refrigerators. More comprehensive multi-battery backups, capable of powering entire homes, come with an even higher price tag: between $22,000 and $40,000. In addition to maintenance costs, these battery backup systems require regular upkeep to ensure they function properly during outages. Homeowners should factor in these ongoing expenses when calculating the total cost of a solar panel system. When selling a home with solar panels, there's an added layer of complexity that buyers must consider. The presence of outstanding financing or power purchase agreements can be a major deterrent for potential buyers who don't want to take on the associated costs and responsibilities. This is because prospective buyers may view the unpaid balance as a liability, potentially affecting their ability to secure a mortgage or qualify for a solar lease themselves. In fact, if the buyer refuses to assume the remainder of the contract, they may be required to pay off the entire balance upfront - an expensive proposition that could derail the sale altogether. To make matters worse, buyers must also meet the leasing company's approval requirements in order to secure the necessary financing for the solar equipment. This can add significant time and paperwork to the home-buying process, with some leases taking up to two months to be approved. Ultimately, homeowners who finance their solar panels through a power purchase agreement or lease may find that they're unable to sell their property quickly or at a fair price due to these unforeseen complications. articles.title: Nitrogen Cycle Discovery Reveals 12.8 Million Tonnes Deposited Annually into Oceans
articles.summary: Researchers have quantified the amount of organic nitrogen deposited from the atmosphere into the world's oceans, revealing an astonishing 12.8 million tonnes annually.
articles.content: A significant discovery has been made about the global nitrogen cycle, highlighting a major component that was previously overlooked. Researchers have quantified the amount of organic nitrogen deposited from the atmosphere into the world's oceans, revealing an astonishing 12.8 million tonnes annually. This represents approximately 27% of total nitrogen deposition in these waters. The study's findings indicate that in areas where nitrogen is scarce, such as the central Atlantic Ocean and Indonesian seas, this atmospheric organic nitrogen makes up roughly half of all nitrogen deposited. The research team's work has far-reaching implications for our understanding of marine ecosystems and their impact on the climate. According to the study, these new insights will reshape how we view nutrient supply in ocean environments. The scientists' conclusions suggest that their findings could have significant effects on ocean ecosystems and global climate patterns. A paper detailing this groundbreaking research has been published under the title "Atmospheric Organic Nitrogen is a Major Nutrient Source to Global Oceans." The study was led by two professors, Yu Jianzhen from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and Fu Tzung-May from the Southern University of Science and Technology. The chemical complexity of atmospheric organic nitrogen (ON) has long hindered efforts to quantify its contribution to oceanic nutrient fluxes. This uncertainty stems from the difficulties in accurately measuring ON, a process often reliant on laborious and error-prone methods. A team of researchers sought to address this knowledge gap by combining innovative measurement techniques with extensive open-ocean and polar marine observations. Their approach involved integrating an advanced atmospheric ON measurement method with global atmospheric chemistry modeling to estimate ON deposition. "Our study demonstrates that atmospheric ON is far from a minor player in marine ecosystems," said Yu, highlighting the significance of this previously overlooked nutrient source. The researchers' cross-disciplinary collaboration enabled them to quantify the crucial biogeochemical link between the atmosphere and marine ecosystems. The team's measurement method allows for simultaneous detection of both aerosol ON and IN, overcoming traditional approaches that often rely on subtracting IN from total nitrogen. This new analytical technique has already shown its potential in filling major gaps in global data sets. The new analytical technique has been applied to a vast array of marine aerosol samples from research cruises around the world. The team analyzed data from 418 samples collected during 21 expeditions that covered diverse oceanic regions, including multiple journeys to the Arctic and Antarctic. This extensive dataset provides the most comprehensive information on atmospheric organic nitrogen (ON) available to date. The researchers found significant variations in ON concentrations among different locations. In some areas, such as the remote Southern Ocean, levels were extremely low, while others, like the Yellow Sea along the Pacific coast, showed much higher amounts of ON. The study revealed that ON made up approximately 30% of total aerosol nitrogen on average. The team used these measurements to refine a three-dimensional atmospheric chemistry model focused on ON. By doing so, they estimated that around 12.8 million tonnes of ON are deposited into the world's oceans every year. This analysis identified biomass-burning emissions as a major contributor to oceanic ON, accounting for nearly half of the annual total. The study also highlighted other significant sources of ON to the oceans, including marine aerosol emissions and imines produced in atmospheric chemical reactions. These non-marine sources combined account for approximately 70% of all ON deposited into the world's oceans annually. The study suggests that atmospheric organic nitrogen plays a significant role in supplying nutrients to global oceans. This external input can stimulate open-ocean productivity, making it an essential factor in marine nutrient dynamics. Changes in these emissions may have significant effects on the ocean's nutrient balance, which could impact marine life and ecosystems. The research emphasizes the importance of considering terrestrial sources as part of the overall nutrient budget for the world's oceans. These findings highlight the interconnectedness of atmospheric and oceanic systems, underscoring the need to account for all potential nutrient inputs when studying marine productivity and ecosystem health.
